compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

A rebar ticket carries no record of which tracker project it syncs into, nor which repos it belongs
to. The current ticket state fields are seeded in `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py:29-81` and declared in
`src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`; neither includes a project. Today the project is only
implicit — recoverable from a bound issue's key prefix in `bindings.json`, and absent entirely for a
ticket that has never been bound. Epic `0e68-41eb-5782-4336` needs it explicit, because a ticket that
is deliberately not synced has no binding to infer from.

## Approach

Add two ticket state fields together, in one edit set: `bridge_project` (string) and `repos` (list of
strings). They are one story rather than two because a field is not usable without its write path,
and splitting them would put two children on `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`.

`bridge_project` is **tri-state**, mirroring the established `file_impact_scope`
undeclared/none/paths pattern (`docs/ticket-model.md:210-212`): absent means legacy, an explicit
empty string means never sync, and a key means sync there. The three states are distinguished so a
pre-feature store is not read as "every ticket is unsynced". Resolution of the absent state is not
implemented here — it belongs to `resolve_project` in the mapping module.

Both fields are written into the CREATE event data by `create_core`
(`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:169-220`), projected by the reducer, and seeded in
`make_initial_state`. Create-time arguments `--bridge-project` and `--repos` are added to all three
write surfaces — CLI (`composer.create_cli`), library (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:79-135`), and MCP
(`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:47-70`). Note the CLI flag loop rejects unknown options strictly
(`composer.py:287-291`), so the new flags must be registered there or they are hard errors.

`bridge_project` is **promote-only**: setting it on a ticket with no binding is allowed, changing it
on a ticket that already holds one is refused. That keeps the change free of any issue-move or
unbind/rebind machinery. `repos` stays freely editable — it never reaches the tracker, so there is no
binding to invalidate.

No schema version bump: `docs/event-schema.md:124-150` states additive fields on an existing event
type do not require one. Types are generated from the schemas (`reducer/_state.py:11-13`), so the
generator is re-run.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`
- `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py`
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py`
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard: a producer/consumer contract test for the event→state path (real
CREATE event fed through the real reducer, no stubbing), plus a real CLI subprocess test for the
argument parsing, since the strict unknown-option rejection is itself part of the mechanism.

- Happy path: `create task "t" --bridge-project REB --repos rebar,api` produces a ticket whose state
  shows `bridge_project == "REB"` and `repos == ["rebar", "api"]` after a full replay.
- Three-state coverage: a ticket created without the flag replays with the field **absent**; one
  created with an explicit empty value replays with `""`. These must be distinguishable — asserting
  the absent case is not merely falsy is the point of the test.
- Cross-surface parity: the same ticket shape results from the CLI, the library, and MCP.
- Failure path: an edit setting `bridge_project` on a ticket that already holds a binding is refused
  with a non-zero exit and the stored value is unchanged; the same edit on an unbound ticket succeeds.
- Collateral invariant: replaying a ticket created before this change yields identical state apart
  from the two new keys.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bridge_project` and `repos` are declared in the ticket state schema, seeded in
      `make_initial_state`, and projected by the reducer; checked by a replay test asserting both on
      a freshly created ticket.
- [ ] `--bridge-project` and `--repos` exist on the CLI, library and MCP create paths and produce
      identical state; checked by a per-surface test comparing the resulting ticket state.
- [ ] The absent, explicit-empty, and set states are distinguishable after replay; checked by a
      parameterized test asserting each of the three separately.
- [ ] Setting `bridge_project` on a bound ticket is refused while setting it on an unbound ticket
      succeeds; checked by a paired test covering both directions.
- [ ] A ticket created before this change replays to the same state apart from the new keys; checked
      by a fixture-based regression test.
